scenes.line1: Why split or merge your tables?
scenes.say: Why do some databases split data into many tables, while others stick it all together? Which approach actually makes your queries faster?

scenes.label: Normalize
scenes.sub: Organize data to cut redundancy, boost integrity.
scenes.say: Normalization means organizing your data to avoid repetition and keep things consistent. It's all about clean, reliable data.

scenes.label: Denormalize
scenes.sub: Combine tables for speed, accept some redundancy.
scenes.say: Denormalization flips that. You combine tables to make reads faster, even if you repeat some info. It's a trade-off for performance.
Normalized tables mean less repeated data and fewer mistakes, but queries might be slower. Denormalized tables run faster reads, but you risk data getting out of sync.

scenes.question: When should you denormalize?
scenes.right: Denormalize for analytics or reporting, not for transactional systems.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap. Should you always denormalize? Nope. Save it for analytics or reporting. For day-to-day transactions, stick with normalization.
